svg.title: DIA-006B · The far bank
svg.desc: An engraved plate of a gorge seen in section. On the near bank stands a short stone pier, 92 million jobs displaced. On the far bank stands a taller pier, 170 million jobs created. No span joins them. Two measuring lines in rust cross the gap, which is drawn to a scale of years: 20 to 30 years for the internet transition, and 40 years, the full width, for the first industrial revolution. A note at the near edge names the 6.1 million US workers who stand closest to it.
svg.text: PART I · SECTION 6 · WHAT'S ACTUALLY AT STAKE
The World Economic Forum projects 92 million jobs displaced
and 170 million created by 2030: net positive, on paper.

text.tspan: the internet transition, before replacement work arrived
the first industrial revolution: UK productivity grew, wages stagnated

svg.text: Nearest the edge: 6.1 million US workers,
4.2% of the workforce. Clerical and administrative,
How wide the gap is for AI
Each course of stone is 10 million jobs. The gap is drawn to the scale of years marked across it.
DIA-006B · More is built on the far side. The last two crossings took 20 to 30 years, and 40.
